changesets.headline: In the AI Chat page template, the chevron on the artifact card now points toward the end of the line in right-to-left layouts, as it does in left-to-right.

In the AI Chat page template, the message list's scrollbar no longer sits under the artifact panel's resize handle. On desktop the chat column keeps a small gap before the handle, so the whole scrollbar scrolls the messages; before, a press on the half of the scrollbar nearest the handle resized the panel. Mobile, where the handle is hidden, is unchanged.

Internal: the touch animator takes `start: 'next-frame'` for a call made in an input event's own task (a key, a click, a pointer, a touch). Such a call from rest starts at the first frame after that task, in Chromium and in WebKit, so a later listener of the same event that holds the page delays the motion instead of letting it skip into its curve. Not exported from the package entry point.

AppShell keeps server-rendered content when a screen is narrower than the server assumed. On a phone, the shell learned its mobile layout in an urgent update right after it hydrated. When the content inside the shell had not hydrated yet, because its code streams in or loads later, React rendered that content again in place of its server HTML: a visitor lost scroll position and focus, and images inside loaded twice. The shell now takes the client's breakpoint answer in a transition, which waits for that content to hydrate. A client-rendered app and a correct `mobileNav.defaultIsMobile` hint behave as before. No API changes.

BottomSheet syncs its focus return target at commit, and no longer copies its stack view during render. A sheet removed after a render React discards, as a suspended transition does, returns focus to its committed `finalFocusRef`.

BottomSheet: when a touch flick closes a sheet, the dim behind it now clears in step with the sheet. Before, the sheet was gone in about a tenth of a second while the dim was still mostly there, and it kept fading for over half a second more. The fade now follows the close spring's own progress. Reduced motion and every other close are unchanged.

Internal: a closing BottomSheet now takes the layer runtime's shared input hold, through its new `focus: 'kept-inside'` mode, instead of its own exit rules. The sheet behaves as before: the page stays live, a sheet that keeps focus takes no click and no key but Tab, and the sheet is inert and hidden once focus leaves.

BottomSheet keeps its snap points and its reactivated entrance in state, and syncs its drag's stop resolver at commit. A render React discards that changes `snapPoints`, as a suspended transition can, no longer changes the stop a released drag rests at.

`astryx build` starts more whole-page ideas from a page template instead of the empty app shell. When build would start an idea on an app shell and search matched no template directly, a fixed decision over the scores build already computes (plus a fixed word table) gives a whole-page probability; at 0.30 or more, the start is build's best-ranked page template. Ideas with an edit phrase keep the shell, and block suggestions do not change. The decision picks only templates build's word tables list, so an integration's own template is never the lifted start; its other results are unchanged.

ChatComposerInput: an empty input keeps its one-line height and takes typing after a page restyle, for example after an open Dialog that holds a SegmentedControl unmounts. Before, its editable area could collapse to 0px, so a click landed beside it and typing did nothing until a reload.

Running any command from a folder that no longer exists now gives a plain error with a `cd` to the nearest existing folder (text and `--json`, code `ERR_PROJECT_REQUIRED`) instead of a stack trace; `--help`, `--version` and `docs` still answer.

The CLI points agents and people to the experimental theme editor for making or changing a theme, labeled experimental each time: the agent block `astryx init` writes (its one theme line, which also keeps extending an imported theme before ejecting one to fork it), one added line in `astryx init`'s next steps (its other steps stay), `astryx --help`, the theme docs (`astryx docs theme`, the author-a-theme guide, in English and Chinese) and the `theme` command's help and summary name `astryx experimental theme editor new <name> --like neutral`, then `editor set` / `editor how`, `theme add <name>` to wire it, and `editor show <name> --png` to look at each change. `theme eject` adds one line, `experimental theme editor new <name> --like <base>` (the ejected theme when it is a built-in base the editor knows and its package is installed, else `neutral`), and `theme palette generate` adds one line, `experimental theme editor set <name> accent <color>`.

`astryx doctor` warns when the `@astryxdesign/core` peer range of a loaded integration, other than the packages of added themes, which `theme-core-peers` already checks, excludes the installed Core (`integration-core-range`). A package made for another Core installs with only a package manager warning, and its components, themes and docs may not work; the warning names the package, its version and range, and the installed Core, and the fix names the release to look for. A project whose other integrations all declare a range that includes its Core gets a passing row naming them; a project where none of them declares one sees no new row. It is a warning, so no project that passed before fails.

`astryx doctor`'s theme stylesheet check no longer fails on a theme's own files when the theme it extends is added too (`theme add d` and `theme add neutral`): a theme source, its build and the editor's generated files only extend the other theme, so they are not asked to import its stylesheet. An app file that imports an added theme's module without its stylesheet still fails the check.

A refusal longer than a pipe holds (64 KiB) reaches a slow reader whole, such as bash `$(…)` or a reader that takes its time: the `--json` envelope stays valid JSON with its code, and the text refusal keeps its last line. The CLI writes its final error output out before it exits. This is a small change to the shared error output, made for the theme editor's long refusals.

No public API function takes an undocumented `__`-prefixed option. `themeBuild()` reads only its documented `out`, `check`, and `iconsSpecifier` options; what `theme build` hands a batch, family, or package-check build now travels through the CLI's own internal path, so `theme build` and `integration pack-check` behave and print exactly as before. A test fails if a hidden option comes back on any exported function.
Internal: Core's English catalog gains `@astryx.comments.linkCopyFailed` ("Failed to copy value to clipboard.") for Lab's Comments. Apps import nothing new.

useContainerReveal keeps revealed content always visible only when the primary pointer is coarse (a phone or tablet). A touchscreen laptop used with a mouse or trackpad now reveals on hover and keyboard focus like any other mouse device. Previously any touchscreen kept the content visible at rest, so a Thumbnail's hover remove button, Markdown heading links, and every app's hover-revealed row actions never hid.

Internal: Core's internal entries add `@astryxdesign/core/internal/shared-context`, which re-exports the shared React context helper so Lab components can share their contexts under a versioned key. Apps import nothing new.
Internal: Core's internal touch entry re-exports its focus-return-on-removal helper for Lab's Tour. Apps import nothing new.

Adds the English strings of the Lab media player (`@astryx.mediaPlayer.*`): control names, spoken times, chapter and marker context, and previous and next track. They are Lab strings shipped in Core's locale file, as Lab ListInput's strings are; they add no public API to `@astryxdesign/core`.

A theme's padding written with `clamp()`, `calc()`, `min()`, `max()` or `var()` with a fallback now builds as written. The theme compiler splits `padding`, `paddingBlock` and `paddingInline` on the spaces between values only, never on a space inside parentheses or quotes, so `padding: clamp(8px, 2vw, 16px)` stays one value instead of becoming broken CSS. No API changes.

The docs playgrounds for TextInput, TextArea, NumberInput, CheckboxInput, Switch, ProgressBar and StatusDot open with realistic values instead of prop-name placeholders, the Heading playground opens as a level-1 heading instead of inheriting Text's sample with `type: 'body'`, and the ButtonGroup, TabList, SegmentedControl and TopNav playgrounds open with named sample items instead of numbered ones.

DateInput, DateTimeInput: a `value` that the app passes at an Enter or blur that keeps a rejected date no longer erases it, so the entry meets WCAG 2.2 3.3.1 (Error Identification). Before, when an app set `value` in the same update as an Enter or blur that kept unreadable, incomplete, nonexistent, or out-of-range date text, as an app does when it restores the date it had before the edit, the field dropped the text, its message, and `aria-invalid`, and reported `null` through `onEntryErrorChange`; a native date control lost its rejection message the same way. Now the text, its rejection, and its message stay at every such Enter or blur, a blur after an Enter included, so the person can correct the entry, and nothing is reported. A later new `value` replaces the text, as before. No app code changes are needed.

DateInput, DateTimeInput: in a standalone field, rejected dates now meet WCAG 2.2 1.4.1 (Use of Color) and 3.3.1 (Error Identification); inside an InputGroup they set `aria-invalid` and are announced. Before, text that is not a date was marked invalid and announced on every keystroke, with no visible message, and Enter or blur reverted it. A native date control flagged each partial year while the year was typed, showed no message, and dropped the rejection when it restored the committed date at blur. Now text that is not a date shows nothing while you type; Enter or blur keeps it in the field and shows "Invalid date" as the field's error status, with `aria-invalid` and one announcement. Its message replaces a caller `status`, as the field's other rejections already do; with `onEntryErrorChange`, a caller `error` status with a message still wins. A native date control's rejection waits for Enter or blur, shows the out-of-range message a typed date shows, under the same `status` rules, and stays shown after the control restores the committed date at blur. A shown rejection stays through an edit that leaves the date wrong or unfinished, and clears once the date is valid or empty. What a form posts does not change: while kept text is not a date, a hidden input posts the committed date under the field's `name`, and the next Enter submits the form.

In a project with integrations, `docs` keeps the integration check results it gathers, with the theme records they include, so a repeated `docs` call reads them back instead of checking every integration again. An edit to a doc topic shows on the very next call. `doctor`'s cache row names `docs` among the commands that keep what they gather.

Once the per-user cache folder exists, `doctor` keeps its three checks that read only files (the docs tree, progressive disclosure and the CLI's docs) beside search's catalogs, and reads each back while every file it read is unchanged, so a later `doctor` skips them (about 0.2 s, more with large integrations). An edit to any doc shows on the very next run. Its cache row names doctor among the commands that keep what they gather, and `doctor --help` no longer calls it read-only.

SideNav, TopNav, Breadcrumbs: a Ctrl-, Cmd-, Shift- or Alt-click on a link in the mobile navigation drawer opens it the way the browser decides, a new tab for instance, and leaves the drawer open. A plain click still closes it, and so does a modified click that the row's own `onClick` cancels, since nothing opens elsewhere. (#8979)
DropdownMenu syncs the refs its show and hide call at commit. After a render React discards, as a suspended transition does, its entrance under a finger holds input as the committed menu says.

NumberInput takes `entryErrorBehavior`, so a form can pass one value to all of its date, time, and number fields. A typed number is complete only at Enter or blur, so both values keep NumberInput's current timing: its rejection, `aria-invalid`, announcement, and `onEntryErrorChange` report appear at Enter or blur, never while a person types. Setting the prop, or FormLayout's `defaultEntryErrorBehavior`, changes nothing a person sees in a NumberInput. Pagination's page box passes `'complete'`, so a FormLayout around it never changes it.

DateInput, DateTimeInput, and TimeInput take `entryErrorBehavior`, and FormLayout takes `defaultEntryErrorBehavior`. The prop sets when a field shows its own entry error, such as a date the calendar does not have or a time outside `min` and `max`. It does not set when validation runs, and it is not React Aria's `validationBehavior`. `'complete'`, the default, keeps each field's current timing. `'blur-or-enter'` holds the message, `aria-invalid`, the invalid styling, the announcement, and the `onEntryErrorChange` report until the person presses Enter or leaves the field; an edit that makes the entry valid or empty still clears the error at once. A field's own prop wins over the form default, a nested FormLayout replaces it, and a Dialog opened from the form starts without it. PowerSearch value editors and Table filter editors keep `'complete'`. The new `EntryErrorBehavior` type names the two values.

Kept catalogs and check results no longer depend on the value of every environment variable when code only lists the variables' names (as a TypeScript transform does). Tools that set a new value per call, such as AI agent harnesses, missed every kept answer on every call; they now hit like any other run. A variable whose value is read still decides the kept answer, including one read inside a kept gather that another one wraps.

Doc examples take an optional `kind: 'demo' | 'setup'` (default `'demo'`), on component, sub-component and function examples. A `setup` example is code that cannot run on its own, such as an app setup file, a server route, or a snippet that uses variables defined elsewhere: `astryx component <Name>` labels it "(setup, code only)", and a docs site shows it as code with no live preview. In `astryx component <Name> --json`, every example carries its `kind`. Any other value fails to load with a message that names both kinds. `astryx docs authoring` explains when to use `setup`.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: a new accent or neutral color keeps the base theme's own secondary text shade on selected items and rows, a dropzone, numbered citations and segmented-control labels while that shade still reads at 4.5:1; it moves only when it no longer does, and the note says it was kept readable. A write that repeats what the base theme already shows is no longer listed as a styled change.

`astryx experimental theme editor`: the app copy in `src/themes/<theme>/` is written exactly as `theme build` of its source writes it (the build header names that source), so `theme build --check` and `astryx doctor` read it as current, and a stable rebuild of it leaves it the editor's (the next change writes it again). A change that fails after its build no longer leaves the refused build in the app copy: the copy is written only once the change is saved.

`astryx experimental theme editor show`: a show that is refused (or fails to render) leaves the app copy in `src/themes/<theme>/` as it was; the copy is written once show succeeds. System files such as .DS_Store in the copy folder no longer stop the copy; a file of yours there does, and `wiring` then gives the steps by hand, naming that file.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: CSS read with the current specifications' grammar.
changesets.body:
- The editor also reads the current specifications' grammar from `@csstools/css-syntax-patches-for-csstree` (a new dependency, pinned). It adds about 0.1 MB unpacked to the install (one 79 KB JSON file, no dependencies of its own), and loads only when the editor checks a CSS value; no other command loads it, and startup is unchanged. A property MDN marks obsolete but the specifications still define, as browsers ship it, is taken: `font-stretch`, so the font shorthand split names a command that works.
- A negative number the current grammar ranges at 0 or more is refused on a part (`line-height -1`, `gap -2px`), with the positive value as the suggestion.
- A `color-mix()` share outside 0% to 100% is refused for tokens, part colors and the color dials, and the mix with the share at its limit is suggested.
- A font size or weight given alone to `font` on a part (`small`, `1rem`, `700`) is suggested as `font-size` or `font-weight`, never as a family.
- A relative color that keeps its channels (`rgb(from red r g b)`) and `light-dark()` with the same color twice are read as that color. A `color-mix()` in a space the editor does not mix in, or a relative color that changes its channels, says so and suggests the nearest color it can work out.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: more refusals and notes that are true.
changesets.body:
- A negative percentage the current CSS grammar ranges at 0 or more is refused on a part (`line-height -50%`, `gap -10%`).
- A `color-mix()` share may be written as any CSS percentage (`5e1%`, `+50%`, `calc(50%)`).
- Line-height tokens (`--text-*-leading`) take a number with no unit, as Core multiplies them by a text size; `1.5em` and `150%` suggest `1.5`.
- `headings` in other letters or as a weight number suggests the word meant (`BOLD` is bold), and a weight number the nearest weight rung (`800` and `900` are heavy), never a lighter one.
- A whole-theme font under fonts set for body and headings says which role fonts it sits under and how to clear them.
- A font one of the editor's own presets leads with (Comic Sans MS) gets no "must load" note.
- `text-size more` or `less` at the end of the dial's range suggests the base font size token, never a size the dial refuses.
- A CSS font value on a part made of keywords (`italic bold`, `bold 1rem`) is split into its longhands, never a family; after the size, the rest is the family, as CSS reads it (`1rem bold` is size 1rem with the family bold).

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: number tokens read as CSS reads them.
changesets.body:
- Only the tokens Core's stylesheet multiplies by a size inside calc() (the line heights) refuse a unit; weight tokens take the font-weight keywords again (`bold`, `normal`), so a theme saved with one stays editable.
- Numbers are read as the browser reads them: `1.5e0`, `+1.5`, `15E-1` and `1.5EM` are numbers, and a `color-mix()` share like `50.%` is refused.
- A CSS font value on a part with a size and line height (`1rem/1.5`) or a size written as math (`calc(1rem + 2px)`) is split into its longhands; a part named twice (`bold bold`) is refused, never written as a family.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: weights on phones, and values read as CSS reads them.
changesets.body:
- Heading and text weights (the `headings` weight dial, `--text-*-weight` tokens) now apply on phones too: they are written into the phone rules the base theme sets, as font families are.
- A token set to `var(--x, <fallback>)` checks the fallback as the token's own kind.
- Size tokens and color channels read numbers as CSS does: `1.px` and `rgb(255. 0 0)` are refused (with `1px` suggested where that is all), and `+4px` and `4e+1px` are taken.
- `vibrancy` suggests the value meant (`MORE` is more, `70%` and `7e1` are 70), and no value when the theme has no color to saturate.
- The `headings` result lists its weights in words, not `[object Object]`.
- The whole-theme and role `font` take a family alone: a size, a weight or a whole CSS font value is refused with the family, and the base size or headings command where it applies.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor set`: when a part does not read the token named, the suggestions name only tokens of the same kind (a weight goes to a weight token, never to a size or a line height). A `var()` fallback is checked wherever it sits (inside `calc()`, `max()`, `color-mix()`), and an empty fallback on a typed token is refused. A size token given a bare number suggests that number in px (`16` → `16px`), and `text-size 20px`, `2e1`, `+20` and `1.25rem` suggest `text-size 20`.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: fallbacks, saved font dials and size suggestions.
changesets.body:
- A part value's `var()` fallbacks are checked against the property (`padding 'var(--nope, red)'` is refused), as token fallbacks are.
- A saved `font` dial that `set` would refuse (a CSS keyword such as `inherit`, a size, a whole CSS font value) is reported with the commands that fix it, and never built.
- A size one slip from a valid one suggests that size: `16 px` and `16pxx` suggest `16px`, `1,5rem` suggests `1.5rem`. `text-size` suggests the nearest size it takes: `20 px` and `125%` are 20, and a size past either end is that end.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: `font math` is accepted as the CSS generic family it is; the generic families are read from the CSS grammar. With an exact `--font-size-base` set, `how 'bigger text'` steps that token (14px to 17.5px) instead of offering a `text-size` the token would mask. A color dial edited by hand to a see-through, system or variable color (`#2563ebcc`, `transparent`, `Canvas`, `var(--x)`) is refused by name with the undo that removes it, instead of building a gray accent. A value typed with full-width characters, a trailing dot or a CSS comment (`１８`, `18.`, `＃2563eb`, `#2563eb /* brand */`) is suggested as the value meant. `set` refuses a `var()` loop that closes through a token in the theme's own `<theme>.theme.ts`. `show` notes each token the theme's own source sets that a whole-theme dial also writes.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: suggestions keep the value meant, and fractional text sizes say how they build.
changesets.body:
- An exact token refused only for how its value was typed (a trailing `;`, a comment, quotes around it, full-width `＃`) suggests that same value, not a stock one.
- A font name that needs quotes (`Font Awesome 6 Free`) on a font token or a part's `font-family` is suggested quoted, as the font dial writes it.
- A fractional `text-size` (`15.5`) is saved as the whole pixel the type scale builds, and the result says so.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`: mode phrases, questions about what is set, the focus ring, and changes by an amount.
changesets.body:
- "The same accent in light and dark" sets both modes, and a trailing "and dark mode only" still makes the theme dark-only.
- A step that cannot move (badges already fully round) says so, with no command that would be refused.
- Questions about what is set now or the choices ("how round are the cards now?", "what are the available corner values") get `show` and the lookup, never a change.
- "Remove the focus outline" sets its width to 0 and says what that costs; "outline offset" and "focus ring offset" set `--focus-outline-offset`.
- "Decrease the radius by 2px" moves the corners from the theme's own radius now (its corners setting applied); a change by an amount on a part points to its current value instead of setting the amount.
- "Caret color" sets `caret-color`; placeholder text and the selection highlight say they have no setting.
- Screen-size, print and device conditions ("below 600px", "on tablets", "the print version") say the editor has no such conditions, instead of reading "600px" as a radius or "tablets" as tables.
- "Text less black" lightens the text.
- Each item of a list keeps its own values: "headings 32px bold, body 16px regular, captions 12px" sets the headings and the body as asked, with no contradiction, and "captions" (no part) takes nothing from its neighbors.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`: a negated mode, the CSS cursor, device words beside an ask, and labels.
changesets.body:
- "Don't touch dark mode, make the accent orange" changes light mode only.
- `cursor: pointer` sets the CSS cursor; only "caret" or "cursor color" is the text cursor's color.
- A device or print word ("cramped on mobile", "when printing") no longer drops the ask: the rest is answered, with a note that the editor has no such conditions.
- A question about one part's state or group ("which parts are in the inputs group", "how round are the cards now?") gets that part's lookup as well as `show`.
- "Not so round" is one step less; "avoid pure black text" picks a near-black; "flat cards, not flat buttons" changes only the cards.
- `NaNpx` and `Infinitypx` are refused as not numbers; `1e3px` is 1000px.
- Labels are the field label part (a checkbox's or switch's own label when named); "visited links" says a link has no visited state set can name.
- Tailwind `border-2` is a 2px border width and `rounded-full` a pill; `.btn-primary { … }` is the primary button only.
- "Remove all my changes" takes back every setting; a question in a script how cannot read gets no guess.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`: "2px rounder" is a change from the corners now, and "all corners like the buttons" copies the buttons' radius.
changesets.body:
- An amount with a comparative ("2px rounder", "2px sharper", "8px larger") is a change from the value now: the theme's corners move from its own current radius (its settings applied, not the base theme's), and a part's corners move from the radius token it reads. Anywhere else ("4px wider") how says set takes the new value instead of setting the amount.
- "All corners like the buttons" sets every other radius token to the one buttons read.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`: a negated dark mode, undo of what is set, typed times and transforms, and the right targets.
changesets.body:
- "Except in dark mode", "but not in dark mode" and "leave dark mode alone" change light mode only; "not pure black" is a near-black and "not pure white" a near-white.
- "Undo the corners" on a theme that sets no corners says there is nothing to undo.
- "animation-duration 0s" is 0ms; "translateY(-2px) on hover" is a transform on hover; "shrink headings by 20%" says set takes the new value; "fade in tooltips" says the tooltip has no motion of its own.
- "Why are my buttons black" is a lookup, never a change; "is my theme valid", "how many dials" and "list every change" get the command that answers them.
- "radius sm/lg", "setRadius(4)" and "½rem" are read as values; "#22c55e in light, #4ade80 in dark" sets the accent for each mode; two-word CSS color names ("midnight blue") are the CSS color.
- "Text on the accent is hard to read" sets the on-accent text color that reads in each mode; "5 lines tall text box" sets the text area's height in lines; "dropdown shadow" is the dropdown's menu; "checkboxes green" is the checked fill.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`: an amount in rem or em with a comparative ("0.5rem rounder") is a change from the value now, counted at a 16px root, and "tighter", "roomier", "looser", "bolder" and "heavier" read as comparatives too. Where how cannot work out the new value, it says to set the value now plus or minus the amount.
`astryx experimental theme editor how`: a confidence gate, and dislikes, take-backs and dark-mode selectors read.
changesets.body:
- When a question is a question ("is the card too round?"), says "tell me" or "but not too", or asks to "stop" something, how gives the lookup and asks for the change in words instead of guessing a write; "explain X" is the lookup of X.
- "I hate the shadows", "skip …" and "not a fan of …" ask for none of it when that is the whole ask.
- A change on one member of a group ("the text area") carries `--only`, so it does not reach the whole group.
- "3 pixels sharper", "take 2px off" and "remove 4px from" move the value down from where it is.
- "darkmode", `html.dark .card {…}` and `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {…}` scope the change to dark mode.
- "Take back the shadow change" and "shadows like before" undo only what the theme sets, else say there is nothing to take back.
- "Pointer cursor on hover" sets the cursor; "opened accordion title" is the open state; "squre" and "eckiger" are square; "cards look flat" adds depth; "darker while being clicked" is the pressed state.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`: every change by an amount or a direction starts from the theme itself, not the base theme. A darker or lighter color starts from the theme's own color in each mode, and says when it is already as dark or as light as it goes; a bigger text size on a part starts from the size the theme set there; a part's corners moved by an amount start from the radius the theme set on it. Token lookups show the theme's own value.
`astryx experimental theme editor how`: the confidence gate works per clause, and a one-mode change never removes a mode.
changesets.body:
- A clause that is a question, a "tell me", a "stop …" or a "don't touch …" holds back only itself: "stop making the buttons so round, make them square" makes them square, "don't explain, just set the accent to crimson" sets crimson, "don't touch spacing, just make text larger" changes only the text. A whole question ("can the cards be rounder?", "are buttons too round?!") gets the lookup; "can you make …" is an ask.
- Questions without a question mark ("are my corners too round", "does it use a shadow on cards") are lookups; suggestions ("why not square buttons", "what about a teal accent", "is there a way to …") are asks. Sarcasm ("yeah, because …", "just what I wanted", "…, nice") gets no write.
- "Enough with X", "quit with X", "nobody asked for X", "who needs X", "loathe X", "X 👎" and "❌ X" ask for none of X; "I hate it" after a description leaves the description as the ask.
- "Too airy" is tighter, "headings too thin" bolder, "not bright enough" brighter.
- "Keep the dark mode accent, change only light to violet" sets the light accent; a light-only or dark-only theme only when the ask is about the theme's modes.
- "Links not underlined until hover" removes the underline and adds it on hover.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor how`: "bolder" or "a bit lighter" headings move one rung from the headings rung the theme sets (and say so when there is no rung further), and "a bit bigger" text moves a numeric text size by the dial's own step. `how <theme> <question>` takes a first word that names an existing theme as the theme, as `set`, `show` and `undo` do.

`astryx experimental theme editor how`: a write only for a direct ask. A clause that is a condition ("if the corners are round, …", "unless …"), an indirect question ("I wonder if …", "is 4px a good radius", "would #333 work", "should corners be 6px or 8px"), a double negative ("don't not round …") or a check ("can you check if …", "just checking: …") gets the lookup and a request to say it as an ask, not a guessed change. Politeness ("if you can, …") is not a condition. `astryx experimental theme editor`: a `dark-only` or `light-only` theme keeps both halves of its colors, and its mode is the one the app's `<Theme>` is given.
changesets.body:
- The theme's colors keep their light and dark values, so a toast, a lightbox or an overlay Core draws in the other mode stays readable; the generated settings module carries only names Core's types take, so the app type-checks.
- `set <theme> mode dark-only` (or `light-only`) says to give the app's `<Theme>` `mode="dark"` (or `"light"`), and the wiring after `theme add` says where it goes; the preview passes it already.
- Settings for the other mode stay out of a one-mode theme and are named, as before.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor new` ends with how to look at the theme after each change: `editor show <name> --png` writes `themes/<name>/preview.png` and `sheet.png` from real components and changes nothing in the app; open the pictures and check them against what was asked.

`astryx experimental theme editor` reads the page-wide tokens of your own `<theme>.theme.ts` however they are written (inline, a const, a spread, `as const` or `satisfies`), from the `defineTheme` the build loads, never a sibling theme in the same file; a value it cannot read in the file comes from the build. The `experimental theme template --overwrite` and `compile --out` help match what they do.
`astryx experimental theme editor`: shorthands by what they set, and part values Core can carry.
changesets.body:
- A shorthand set after its longhands replaces only the longhands it really sets, read from MDN's data (`overflow` keeps `overflow-wrap`, `transform` keeps `transform-origin`, `flex` keeps `flex-direction`), and a part's `background` keeps reaching its variants when `background-blend-mode` comes later.
- A group's shorthand replaces its members' longhands as a part's does, so the later setting wins either way.
- On a part whose padding Core writes one variable per side (card), a variant's padding after a side set for every variant is refused, with the commands that work: it would not show.
- `--on cards`, `dialogs`, `tabs` and other plurals name the part, with the set command.
- Word hints keep the value given: `shadow none` is `box-shadow none`, `rounded 8px` is `corners 8px`, `bold false` is `font-weight normal`.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: card padding and radius written exactly.
changesets.body:
- On a part whose padding Core writes one variable per side (card and the other containers), the editor writes each side itself, split as CSS splits a shorthand: `calc(4px + 2px) 8px`, `clamp(12px, 2vw, 24px)` and four different sides reach the part as typed.
- A variant's padding after a side set for every variant now shows: the editor writes the variant's side variables too, instead of refusing it.
- A card radius of more than one value (`12px 12px 0 0`, `10px / 20px`) gives each corner its own radius; the content that reaches the card's edges takes one radius, the first corner's, and the result says so.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: variant values win over lifted base values, and card padding keywords written exactly.
changesets.body: - A part's base value lifted onto a variant (so Core's own variant rule does not hide it) now goes before the variant's own declarations, so a longhand or shorthand set for the variant wins (`border-color` for the destructive button after a base `border`).

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: padding sides and inner radii that win as written.
changesets.body:
- A later part padding replaces a side its group set.
- A part's own multi-value radius keeps the content's radius it gives over a single radius from a group, a dial or the base theme's lifted onto a variant.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: the chat composer's box is reached as it is drawn.
changesets.body: - `padding` on chat-composer goes to the padding of the visible composer box, with no gap outside it. Background, border, shadow, a side padding or a padding for one density, which would land on the composer's transparent wrapper, are refused with the reason.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: one padding model for parts whose box reads Core's padding variables.
changesets.body:
- On card, clickable-card, selectable-card, dialog, drawer, bottom-sheet, section and number-input, each part's padding is worked out per variant and per state from every padding setting in the order made, side by side for each text direction (a physical left is the start in a left-to-right box and the end in a right-to-left one; so is the `padding` shorthand's left), and written to the variables the box reads. The later setting wins in both directions, a variant or a state out-ranks the base, and the content that reaches the box's edges stays in line.
- A clickable or selectable card is padded as a card.
- A part's base rules come before its variants', and its rules for a direction before its states', whatever order the settings were made in.
- `padding` on chat-composer takes one length, as Core reads it inside calc(): a length, a variable such as `var(--spacing-3)` (Core's own default), or `calc()`, `min()`, `max()` or `clamp()` giving one. Several values, a bare number or a percentage is refused with one that works.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: padding that stays where it is set, and one length wherever Core reads it inside calc().
changesets.body:
- Padding set on a clickable or selectable card, or on a card's variant or state, no longer reaches plain cards nested inside it: each side the narrower rule writes is reset on a plain card inside it, so Core's own fallback holds, and the narrower rule writes each side rather than the whole padding.
- Every part whose padding Core reads inside calc() (found from Core's own stylesheet: chat-composer, dropdown-menu, context-menu, segmented-control, and an item's inline padding) takes one length there, as chat-composer does, also through a group (`--on menus`).
- A padding with `--state` on a card, dialog or a group of containers is now taken: the padding model writes the state's own sides.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: nested sections that follow their parent, and lengths Core can calculate with.
changesets.body:
- A section padding the same on every side is written as the section's whole padding, which Core reads after the padding a parent section passes down, so nested sections keep following their parent.
- A padding of `0` is written as `0px` on parts where Core calculates with it (card, section, dialog, drawer, bottom-sheet); `initial` and `unset` leave the padding to Core's own default.
- A hand edit to the settings file that `set` would refuse is reported by the next `set` with the command that removes it, as `compile` does, instead of being built.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a part's padding replaces the base theme's, and every padding writes a length Core can calculate with.
changesets.body:
- A padding on a card, section, dialog, drawer, bottom-sheet or number-input replaces the base theme's padding there, whichever sides the base theme set: the editor writes it as padding properties Core works out together with the base theme's, where the later one wins.
- A clickable or selectable card's padding wins over a card's left or right padding in each text direction.
- A plain part nested in a narrower one is reset only on the sides its own rule leaves unset, so a padding in your own theme source on that part still applies.
- A zero written any way (`0e0`, `0.0`) is written as `0px`; `initial` and `unset` name the part's own default padding from Core.
- A hand-edited padding on one part is reported when a `set` changes padding on another part too.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: what the editor builds, `compile --check` takes.
changesets.body:
- Two to four corner radii on card, button, dialog, avatar, banner, popover and the other parts with an inner-corner radius are written as CSS properties Core reads (the whole radius, which Core turns into the content's radius, then each corner), never as a private variable, so `compile` and `compile --check` pass.
- A padding on chat-composer is refused with the reason: the box inside its transparent wrapper reads its padding only from a variable of Core's own, which a theme cannot set, and a padding on the wrapper would add a gap outside the box.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a padding in your own theme source wins over the editor's on the same part, whatever sides each names.
changesets.body:
- A padding your `<theme>.theme.ts` sets on a part's plain rule, a variant or a state wins over an editor padding there (`padding 20px --on card` under your own card padding of 6px shows 6px), and the result says so, also right after an edit to that file, before any build.
- An editor padding on a part's plain rule that differs by text direction keeps the plain rule's weight, so any variant, your own included, out-ranks it.
- `padding inherit` (and `revert`) on parts whose padding Core keeps in its own variables is taken like `initial` and `unset`, and the result names the default it means.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: the spacing dial keeps the small, medium and large control sizes apart and in order at every step.
changesets.body: - A denser spacing still makes controls shorter by the plain scale, but no size meets the one below it: one that would keeps its own step, scaled, above it, and none goes under 24px (`spacing tight` on Neutral gives 24px, 27px and 30px, where small and medium both ended at 24px). The dial's help says control heights follow it.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: every picture `--png` takes carries the editor's stamp (a PNG text chunk naming the theme), so it is known as the editor's even without its record; a picture an earlier version took, with no record yet, is taken over when it is the editor's 1280-pixel window, and the result says so once. Only links among the files the editor reads or writes are refused, each named with where it points; a link to a file of yours (notes, a mockup) is left alone. A `new` refused for its name leaves out of its suggestion a vibrancy that would change nothing (no color given), and says so. The `--png` help of new, set, show and undo names the picture record and when no picture is taken.

`astryx experimental theme preview`: the route and pages it writes type-check with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noImplicitOverride` and `noUnusedLocals`. `add --path` refuses a folder name that is no plain URL segment (a space, an accent, `#`, `%`), suggesting a slugged one. Folder names Windows does not allow are refused in full: reserved characters, a trailing dot or space, and `COM¹`-style device names. The free folder a URL conflict suggests is one whose URL no other page serves. `preview app` leaves out a temp file a stopped command left in the theme folder.

`astryx experimental theme preview`: in the preview's nav, only a plain left click switches the page in place; a Ctrl/Cmd, Shift, Alt or middle click opens the page's URL as a link does. The `see` line after an editor change now leads with a look that changes nothing in the app (the editor's own `preview.html`, current after every change it renders, and `--png`), then the in-app preview page when there is one; adding the preview to the app comes last, as an option.

`astryx experimental theme preview add`: a folder name that Next serves at a plain URL (letters, digits and `. _ ~ ! $ & ' ( ) + , ; = @ -`) is accepted. For any other name, every odd segment is slugged and the suggested folder is a free one. A folder that differs from another only in case is refused, since macOS and Windows treat them as one. In an app with no TypeScript, the result names the install line. When the app's tsconfig turns on `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, the result names the template pages written as their template ships. The Colors page shows a seed color as it is stored.

`astryx experimental theme`: going back to the preview's bare URL shows its first page, as a reload does. `editor undo` points its `see` line at the page about what it reverted. A preview whose URL depends on the app's routing, or whose folder was renamed by hand, is named where it is, by `see` and by `preview list`, instead of suggesting a new one. `preview add --theme` takes a pasted label (`theme: t`, `name: t`) as the theme t; an editor command given one refuses it and suggests `show t`. A change the editor could not render says why in its `see` line instead of pointing at a `preview.html` it did not write.

`astryx experimental theme preview`: a default page's id beside another page asked for is refused ("drop one of them") instead of dropping the other. `preview add colors` on a theme with no generated colors says how to get them. `preview list` marks a page whose file is gone and notes a change that was stopped part way, and `add` writes a missing page back as added. Running a stopped `preview remove` again finishes it and exits 0. `basePath` is certain only when set as a literal on the exported config at the top of next.config; one set in an `if` or a function, deleted, or added by a wrapper is named as set from code.

`astryx experimental theme preview`: the preview route renders its pages only in the browser, so a component that crashes a server render no longer stops `next build` when Components is the first page. next.config is read the way Next loads it: `.js` before `.mjs`, `.mts`, `export {config as default}`, a key set after the object, and the last of a repeated key; a config changed in other ways gets a note instead of a guess. Table pieces (TableHeader, TableBody, TableFooter) are no longer shown alone on the Components page. `preview add overview` (or another default page's id) brings back the default pages that are missing.

`astryx experimental theme preview app --theme <t>`: the new app installs the Core and base theme versions this project has, the ones the copied build was made on, so the theme is current after install; a note names them and how to move to this CLI's release.

`astryx experimental theme preview`: `add` rebuilds the theme whenever its build is not current (an output missing, or a build that does not match the settings), the same rule `preview app` uses, so the route never imports a missing file. A pasted `--theme 'theme: t'` names the theme t. A `distDir` with a subfolder blocks only that folder. `remove --path` on a folder with no preview names the preview there is, with its remove. The `preview app` help says that with `--theme` Core and the base theme are pinned to the project's versions.

`astryx experimental theme`: every in-app preview page has its own URL (`/theme-preview?page=components`), which the nav links to, so a link, a reload, the back button or a screenshot reaches any page; `preview add`, `list` and `app` give each page's URL. Every editor change carries a `see` line: first a look that changes nothing in the app (the editor's `preview.html`, current after the change, and `--png`, which takes pictures with no dev server), then the in-app preview page most about it (Colors after a color, Components after a part, Overview otherwise) at its URL when there is a preview, and adding one last, as an option. The `--png` help says it needs a Playwright or a Chrome and adds a few seconds.

`astryx experimental theme preview`: a `--path` that goes through a file, has a folder name longer than 255 bytes, or is longer than 3,500 bytes, is refused with a reason. A folder that differs from another only in case is refused for `preview app` and for a `--path` outside the routes folder too. `preview remove` leaves a page file it cannot read in place, says so and keeps it recorded. A preview flag given twice with different values is refused.

`astryx experimental theme preview remove`: a page the app's own code imports is kept, and the importing file is named, for one page and for the whole preview. The check reads the whole project, following relative imports, `@/` and tsconfig path aliases.

`astryx experimental theme preview`: popovers shown open on the Overview and Components pages no longer take focus, so the page stays where it opened. The Overview points to the Colors page only when the preview has one, and a color `set` on a theme whose preview has no Colors page says which `preview add` adds it. `preview remove` takes away the empty folders the preview's first `add` made, never one that was there before. The Overview reads its font line again when the theme changes while the page is open. The `preview app` starter lists `@types/node`, so its first `npm run dev` installs nothing.

`astryx experimental theme preview add`: an app frame's exact name as the description (`blank`, `shell-top-nav`) is refused with a clear reason and the `--template` command. An exact template name is called the page named, not the closest page. With no routes folder, the refusal names the Next apps below with a `--path` into each, and a `--path` that would make a routes folder with no root layout is refused before writing. Page packages are read from the app the preview is in. The Core stylesheet check starts from the root layout over the preview, route groups included, and follows tsconfig path aliases.

`astryx experimental theme preview add`: a short description that names a page template (`checkout`, `hero`, `a landing page`) takes the page `build` ranks first, instead of being refused. A description that is exactly a template's id or display name adds that page, or says why it was skipped. The Core stylesheet note follows the root layout's imports, so a stylesheet imported from a root `styles/` file counts. A theme font whose package the app lacks gets a note with the install line, and the Overview marks a font that is not installed.

`astryx experimental theme preview remove`: the check that keeps a page your code imports now reads the whole project (every source file outside installs, build output and dot folders), parses each file's imports, exports, `import()` and `require()` calls, template-string ones included, and also guards the route a file re-exports. A project too big to check is refused rather than half-checked. A route changed by hand is told to move out of the preview folder. `preview add --template overview|components|colors` adds just that page when it is missing, or says why not. Temp files a stopped preview command left are cleaned by the next one and by a full remove.

`astryx experimental theme preview`: when both spellings of a folder are already there, the case-clash refusal suggests a new folder beside them, and names `preview remove` for a preview already inside. A `theme-preview.json` entry that leads outside the folder (`../`) is reported as damaged by `add` and `list`. `remove` drops such an entry and deletes nothing outside, and its messages show paths from the project.

`astryx experimental theme preview`: the route of a one-mode theme no longer imports the mode switch it does not draw, so apps with `noUnusedLocals` build. A refused `--theme` says exactly what leaving it out does in this app: the theme the preview keeps wearing, or the one theme under `themes/` it picks.

`astryx experimental theme preview`: no demo on the Components page takes focus as it mounts. A dialog part such as DialogHeader shows inside an open inline Dialog, and an open Popover is named. When the preview's theme is gone, its Colors page goes with it. `preview remove` refuses while a file of yours in the folder imports the preview pages, and its advice for a route changed by hand is to move it out of the folder. `preview list` with no preview says why `add` would refuse the folder instead of suggesting it. `remove` takes away the empty folders `add` made outside the routes folder too. Every page-template list suggestion names the command the way the app runs the CLI, in `--json` as in text.

`astryx experimental theme preview`: the base theme's fonts stylesheet is imported only while the theme's build still names a family it loads, so a theme on `font system` or its own fonts fetches nothing it does not use. `preview add` names every page it writes again, the Colors page included, when the preview switches theme.

`astryx experimental theme preview`: `add --path` refuses an intercepting route folder (`(.)x`, `(..)x`, `(..)(..)x`, `(...)x`), where a page breaks the whole app. The preview loads the fonts stylesheet of the theme it is built on (Figtree for neutral), and so does the `preview app` starter, so the Overview shows the family it names. `preview list` text marks a page whose file is gone as missing, matching `--json`.
`astryx experimental theme`: padding sides by direction, a failed show leaves the folder as it was, and `how` reads "not dark enough".
changesets.body:
- On dropdown-menu, context-menu and segmented-control, one logical padding side is written for each direction (the left in a left-to-right box, the right in a right-to-left one), so it changes that side only; under a state it is one rule per direction (`:hover:dir(ltr)`), and a later padding or physical side replaces it.
- `show` whose render fails puts back every output it touched, removing one it made new and restoring the palette files in `tokens/`.
- `how "not dark enough"` / `"not light enough"` asks for darker or lighter, not for one mode.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: a card's physical padding side beside others, a failed show beside your own folders, and the busy-lock suggestion from the API.
changesets.body:
- A card `padding-left` or `padding-right` set beside another side, as a keyword (`initial`) or as math (`calc()`), reaches that side.
- `show` whose render fails leaves a folder you put in `tokens/` alone.
- When another command holds the theme, the suggestion to run again names the call's own command with every option it got (`--only`, `--like` and each dial of `new`, `--png`), never the arguments of the process the API runs in; a preview command waiting on another names `preview list`.

changesets.headline: `astryx experimental theme editor`: every `set` a refusal suggests is now checked the way `set` checks it, without writing anything, and a suggestion `set` would refuse is left out. Suggestions carry what was asked instead of a fixed example. `headings light --on heading` offers `headings light` and weight 300 on one level. `text-size large --on card` offers that size on the card. A number token reads the number meant (`700px` is 700, `1,5` is 1.5, `calc(1rem+2px)` gets its spaces). A word dial given a number offers its own words, or the nearest `type` preset for a scale ratio. An invalid color is never copied into the text color token. A color property refuses a `var()` fallback inside `color-mix()` that is not a color. `how "more washed out colors"` lowers vibrancy.

In a project where no integration can load (no Astryx config, no integration manifest of its own, and no installed dependency that ships one), help and commands that don't need the project no longer load it first just to read the commands integrations declare: `--help`, `manifest` and `blog` answer about 65 ms sooner. Output is unchanged.

Hook docs for `useOutlineFromDOM`, so `astryx hook useOutlineFromDOM` and `astryx search` return it, and a `useOutlineFromDOM — Article` example block: an article and an Outline built from its headings through the hook, with a button that adds a section and its linked entry.

Icon sets: a project picks one look for every icon. `astryx experimental icon use <main> --variant <variant>` writes `experimental.iconVariant` beside `experimental.iconSet`, in one write, and refuses a variant the main set does not declare; without `--variant` it removes the key. Each set in the list draws its variant of that name, or its default look when it declares none, and the receipt (`icon.use`) adds `variant`, `previousVariant`, `looks`, and `themeMap`. A copied template imports each icon in that look where its set has it, reports the look as `icons.variant`, and moves an icon a template imports from the main set's own library, or from a listed set in another look (`by: 'variant'`), to that look. A set's generated module also writes a theme map for each other look an icon draws (`themeIconsFilled`), and `integration check` holds it to `map`. `astryx doctor` fails when the main set does not declare the variant, and `experimental icon --list` shows the variant and each set's look. A CLI before 0.7.16 refuses an astryx.config that sets `experimental.iconVariant`, so `use` warns when the project's CLI range admits one. An icon-set package whose generated module an earlier CLI wrote, and whose icons draw a look other than the default, fails `integration check` until it runs `experimental icon add --variant <variant> --from <module> --all` again; the finding names that run. Projects that do not set `experimental.iconSet` see no change.

In forced-colors mode (Windows contrast themes), `primary` and `secondary` Buttons gain a `ButtonText` border, and `destructive` keeps its `CanvasText` border; in a connected `ButtonGroup` the solid buttons keep the group's dividers and close the group's outer edge, with no doubled seam. Floating surfaces that separate from the page with a box shadow alone gain a `CanvasText` border: `Popover` and every surface `usePopover` paints (including `DropdownMenu`), `DropdownMenuSubMenu` flyouts, `ContextMenu`, and an `isInline` `Dialog`. Forced colors removes fills and box shadows, which left these controls and surfaces without an edge. The borders exist only in forced colors, so nothing changes elsewhere. A theme that sets a solid variant's own border width keeps it, so Gothic's `secondary` Button stays borderless.

`astryx doctor integration validate` and `astryx integration check` name unreachable contribution metadata with forward slashes on every platform. On Windows the path in "Found contribution metadata ... outside every declared integration root" used backslashes, while the fix in the same message used forward slashes.

A kept entry in the per-user cache whose value is missing or has the wrong shape for what it holds is now worked out again and stored over, instead of being used: a damaged entry could make `search`, `doctor` or `template --list` fail until the folder was cleared.

In a project with integrations, each integration's discovered themes are kept beside search's catalogs and read back while every file they read is unchanged, so `theme list` and the other theme commands skip re-reading an integration's themes on later calls (about 0.1 s with a large integration). An edit to a theme, or to a module it imports, shows on the next run. `doctor`'s cache row names the kept theme records.

In a project with integrations, the whole integration issue list is kept beside search's catalogs (the template and component replacement checks over Core and every integration, as well as each integration's own checks) and read back while every file it read is unchanged, so `component`, `template`, `theme` and `search` skip those passes on later calls (about 0.1–0.25 s each with a large integration).

In a project with integrations, template discovery's records are kept beside search's catalogs and read back while every file and folder discovery read is unchanged, so `template --list`, `template <name>` and `build` skip discovering templates on later calls (about 0.1 s with a large integration), and a template added, renamed or edited in an integration shows on the next call. A record that would not read back exactly (a function, a Map, a shared object, -0 and the like) is never kept. `doctor`'s cache row names template discovery's records.
A layer with several triggers now opens at another trigger when the press on that trigger is the one that closes it, with a mouse or a finger. A press on the open trigger still closes it.

An anchored layer flush against its trigger, or over its edge, no longer slides over it: its entrance scales in place, as it does for a layer over its trigger's center. A menu at the pointer still slides from the side it lands on.

An anchored layer that has room to its trigger no longer starts its entrance over it: its first step toward the trigger stops at that room. So a tall tooltip 4 px beside its trigger no longer covers it on its first frame in Safari.

The layer runtime syncs its close-start and replayed-show refs at commit, not during render, and its keep-open press reads the committed open state or the shown layer. A render React discards no longer leaves its values for later callbacks.

A light-dismiss layer opened while a press is released no longer closes at that release. A DropdownMenu or ContextMenu row that opens a Popover when chosen with a mouse now leaves it open, as it already did with a finger; the next press outside, or Escape, closes it as before.

Importing `@astryxdesign/cli/api`, as integration codemods and other integration code do, no longer loads Babel, recast, jscodeshift and postcss-selector-parser up front: each loads the first time it is used (about 0.25 s and 350 fewer modules per import). The API's exports are unchanged.
A mouse click on the dark space beside a Lightbox photo now closes the viewer. Before, the viewer stayed open after a click there within the photo's natural width, or within a wider caption's width.

A Lightbox gallery's caption sits in a band two lines tall under every photo, so the photo keeps one size and place from item to item. A photo with no caption keeps the band's space without its backing. A longer caption shows two lines, the second ending in an inline "more" link, which opens the whole caption over the photo. The whole caption is always the viewer's accessible description.
changesets.body: The viewer is a media surface: its controls, caption and counter take the theme's dark surface tokens through `MediaTheme`. The caption is body `Text` whose lines start at one edge, "more" and "less" are `Link`'s button form in the caption's own type, and the band clears the screen's bottom edge and its safe area. A gallery's caption sits on a backing that keeps it at 4.5:1 over any photo. A tap that opens the viewer paints no focus ring on its first control, and paging from a focused "more" or "less" keeps focus in the viewer.

changesets.headline: A single photo's caption in a `Lightbox` now shows as a gallery's does. It sits in the band at the bottom of the viewer, on the caption's backing, which keeps 4.5:1 over any page behind it. The photo centres above it. A caption longer than two lines ends in "more", which opens it in full over the photo. A single photo with no caption shows no band.
ListItem's `startContent` and `endContent` docs now say that the content sits inside the row, before the label or after the label and description, not before or after the item.

When a reorderable `List` row does not render again, its handle's name still follows it. A handle named after its place ("Reorder item N") follows that place when rows above it go or the rows reorder. A label that gains or loses its text renames the handle.
Internal: Markdown notes why its parser caches cannot show a discarded render's text, with a test that a discarded streamed render never shows its text.

Markdown text transforms that declare `requiredSubstrings` look for those substrings in one pass over the source. Before, each paragraph searched the rest of the document again, so long Markdown (such as a long streamed chat answer) rendered more slowly with each paragraph. Output is unchanged.

DropdownMenu, ContextMenu, Selector, TabList, TopNav, SideNav, Breadcrumbs: when a finger picks a menu row, the click guard cancels only that finger's `touchend` once the menu has named the touch, so another finger's `touchend` passes. The menu names the touch from the `touchstart` that follows its `pointerdown`. A `touchend` without `changedTouches`, or a lift whose touch the menu could not name, keeps the old rule: the next `touchend` is cancelled.

MetadataList's guidance now says that assistive technology reads each label with its value, and that the title does not name the list or add a heading. Its prop docs now list `className` and `style`, and the `label` docs say that `position: 'start'` places a label at the inline start of its value, not on the left.

MoreMenu, InfoTip, PowerSearch (with its PowerSearchToken and PowerSearchFilterEditor defaults), Toast, and InputClearButton now pass host `data-*` attributes to their own element, as other components do: the trigger button for MoreMenu and InfoTip, the primary control for PowerSearch, the token and editor root for the PowerSearch defaults, the toast element for Toast, and the button for InputClearButton. Component-owned attributes stay with the component. A new test renders every exported component that renders an element of its own with a `data-*` attribute, and fails when the attribute does not reach the DOM.
`component --list` finds a component that has no folder of its own about 20 ms sooner: one index of Core's folders replaces a check of each folder in turn. Output is unchanged.

Internal: Neutral's palette receipt names the generator and candidate format versions, as every other official theme's receipt does, so it matches the receipt its config regenerates. No color, token or digest changes.

`astryx docs styling/tokens-and-setup` has a Next.js with webpack section. It shows `experimental.optimizePackageImports: ['@astryxdesign/core']` in `next.config.mjs` and recommends a component entry, such as `@astryxdesign/core/Button`, in Server Components.
