NumberInput: `onEntryErrorChange` reports why the field rejects typed text, so an app can word its own message. It receives a `NumberInputEntryError` with a `kind` that does not depend on the locale (`unreadable`, `fractional` for a fraction when `isIntegerOnly`, or `outOfRange` for any number while `min` is above `max`), the typed `text`, and, for `fractional` and `outOfRange`, the number as `value`. It runs each time the rejection changes: at Enter or blur, when an edit makes the text valid or empty, when a new `value`, `min`, `max`, or `isIntegerOnly` changes or ends it, and when disabling the field drops the text. It reports `null` when the rejection ends, or when the field unmounts while one stands, and never twice for the same rejection. Pass an `error` `status` with a message to word the rejection; that message is the one announced.

NumberInput: a rejected entry now shows a message and stays in the field, so the field meets WCAG 2.2 1.4.1 (Use of Color) and 3.3.1 (Error Identification). Before, every draft that was not an accepted number, an unfinished one such as `-` included, set `aria-invalid` and was announced on each keystroke, while the text only turned secondary; blur then reverted a draft that did not parse, with no message. Now nothing is marked or announced while a person types, because a typed number is complete only at Enter or blur. At Enter or blur, text that is not a number, a fraction when `isIntegerOnly`, or any number while `min` is above `max` stays in the field: the field shows "Invalid number" as its error status, tied to the input by `aria-describedby`, sets `aria-invalid`, and announces it once. Inside an InputGroup the rejection sets `aria-invalid` and is announced. An edit that makes the draft valid or empty clears it at once. A number outside an ordinary range still clamps and commits through `onChange`. A caller `error` status with a message still shows in place of the field's message; a `warning` or `success` status no longer hides a rejection. What a form posts does not change: while blur keeps a rejected draft, a hidden input posts the committed number as the field showed it before. Pagination's `input` variant shows the message on its page box's status icon and widens the box beside the typed text while a rejected entry stays, so the bar keeps its height. No app code changes are needed.

`astryx theme palette generate` and `generateTonalPalette()` honor `darkChromaTaper`, so every official theme palette regenerates from its saved config exactly as committed. Neutral's config asks for a muted dark edge on its chromatic families, but the generator dropped the field: 99 of Neutral's 420 colors came out more saturated than the committed ones (`blue.dark[25]` was `#003978`, not `#253c5a`). A dark stop now keeps `edgeMultiplier` of its in-gamut chroma through `throughStop`, then recovers along a smoothstep to the standard recipe at `recoverAtStop`; `familyMultipliers` sets the edge share for one family. Light ramps, neutral families, the black and white endpoints, and configs without the field generate the same colors as before. A taper with a field it does not read, a stop outside the layout, a family the request does not have, a neutral family, or a multiplier outside 0 to 1 is refused.

Pasting into a `RichTextEditor` table no longer drops the paste or empties cells. A pasted table fills the cells one by one from the caret's cell, or within the selected cells. A merged cell in it fills only the cell where it starts instead of emptying the cells it covered, and a table whose rows differ in length arrives whole. A table pasted together with other content, as a web page copies it, goes into the cell as text instead of being discarded.

Under a finger, a Popover that overlaps its trigger now grows from where it meets the trigger, as the pointer entrance does. A popover a few pixels over its trigger's side grows from that side, not from below. A popover over its trigger's center grows from that center by scale only. Every other landing grows as before.

`astryx experimental render` says why a page ended without an answer: the stage it reached (such as importing the page or rendering on the server), how long it ran, the memory left, and the page's last error output. A page process that loses its channel or reaches its own time limit is reported as that, never as a clean exit.
Toast announces the rendered message when a body's text comes only from a component, and from custom layouts (#7853)

A link typed without a scheme, whose host has a dot or is `localhost`, followed by a port, such as `example.com:8080`, `www.example.com:8080/docs` or `localhost:3000`, now gets the default `https://` like `example.com` does, instead of being read as an unknown scheme and turned into `about:blank`

New message `@astryx.richTextEditor.link.urlPlaceholder` ("example.com"), the placeholder of the RichText toolbar's link field. The descriptions of the other `@astryx.richTextEditor.link.*` messages and `@astryx.richTextEditor.toolbar.link` now describe the link popover that replaces the link dialog; their messages are unchanged.

`RichTextEditorToolbar`'s Link button, and Cmd/Ctrl+K in the editor, open a popover anchored to the button instead of a modal dialog. The popover holds one URL field, applied with Enter, and Apply, Remove (when the selection is in a link), and Cancel icon buttons with tooltips. It is not modal: Escape or Cancel closes it and returns focus and the selection to the editor, and a URL that cannot be linked shows an error under the field, which keeps focus. The URL rules (`sanitizeUrl`), `hasNewTabLinks`, and `promptForUrl` are unchanged; with `promptForUrl` the Link button opens no popover, as it opened no dialog.
changesets.body: The popover opens above the toolbar and flips below it only when there is no room above. Apply and Cancel use the shared `check` and `close` icons, so a theme that restyles those icons restyles them too; Remove's glyph is fixed artwork. `RICHTEXT_ICON_KEYS` is unchanged.

changesets.headline: SegmentedControl: where the control has no layout, as in a unit test's DOM, a click on a later segment keeps that segment selected instead of switching to the first segment a moment later. Browsers are unaffected.
Selector's presentation syncs its show, hide and popover-content refs at commit. After a render React discards, as a suspended transition does, opening the popover runs the committed show.

Internal: a Core component's own drag runs on the shared drag path. `createPan` and `createSnapDrag` take a begin gate, a drag model and a custom property to draw into, beside the public `createPanGesture` and `createDragToSnapPoints`. The animator draws `x` into a registered custom property. Not exported from the package entry point.

Slider syncs its values, change-end callback and touch update refs at commit. After a render React discards, as a suspended transition does, a press on the track reports the committed value to the committed `onChangeEnd`, and a finger dragging a thumb reports to the committed `onChange`.

`theme build`: the refusal for a quoted glob keeps `--family` and `--family-key` in a family run, and builds its suggestion with the same builder as the build's other refusals of a source; the experimental compile's refusals for the editor's settings file and for a subfolder keep `--out` (rebased onto the app root for the `cd` one), so the suggested check reads the output you asked about. (Minimal change to shared code: `buildSuggestion` gains an optional shape for a glob or a family run, and the build command passes `--out` to a group's preflight.)

The published CLI reads the icon definitions and built-in theme descriptors it ships from values stored at publish instead of parsing each file, so `docs` answers about 45 ms sooner and `doctor` and `theme list` about 10 ms sooner. An edited or unknown descriptor is parsed as before. Output is unchanged.
A new example block shows `useTableColumnsVirtualization`: a 121-column Table with a pinned first column that mounts only the columns near its horizontal scroll position.

Column windowing keeps focus and place: with `useTableColumnsVirtualization`, a focused cell whose column scrolls out of the window stays mounted with its original element until focus leaves the table, moves to another cell, or its column is removed, when focus returns to the Table's scroll area. Focus in a menu that a cell opens keeps the cell's column too. Changing column order, widths, visibility or pinning keeps the first visible column and how far it is scrolled. Tables that do not opt in are unchanged.

Tables can window their columns: pass `useTableColumnsVirtualization({initialViewportWidth})` to `Table.virtualization`. Table keeps every column definition and width, mounts only the unpinned columns near the inline viewport plus two overscan columns per side, keeps pinned columns mounted, and gives mounted cells full-table `aria-colindex` values with `aria-colcount` on the table. When the scroll area is at least as wide as the table's minimum width, every column mounts. `Table.virtualization` also accepts a list with at most one rows and one columns capability. Unsupported content or structure renders every column with a development warning. Adding or removing the columns capability remounts the table. Tables that do not opt in render as before; their Table import carries about 0.5 KB gzip of column windowing wiring, and the column planner loads only with the hook.

Add Table infinite loading with `useTableInfiniteScroll({hasMore, isLoading, onLoadMore})`. One Promise request latch coordinates automatic and manual loading, failures pause automatic retry, and the persistent busy Button owns progress announcements and focus continuity.

Tables can window rows and columns together: pass both `useTableRowsVirtualization` and `useTableColumnsVirtualization` to `Table.virtualization` as a list. Table mounts only the cells near the viewport on both axes, keeps full-table `aria-rowindex` and `aria-colindex` values, and keeps a focused cell's row and column mounted while either scrolls away. Tables that do not opt in are unchanged.
Table: `useTableSortableState` calls the `onSortChange` of the last committed render. Before, a sort click during a transition that had not committed yet called the callback from that pending render.

TextArea `htmlMaxLength` sets the native `maxlength` attribute, so a form can cap typing in UTF-16 code units, including an SSR form before hydration. It is independent of `maxLength`, the soft counter, which still counts user-perceived characters and never blocks typing. TextArea adds no truncation or validation of its own, and renders no native `maxlength` when `htmlMaxLength` is unset.

`astryx experimental theme editor` counts a base theme as installed only when the project installs it, in its `node_modules` folders or through Yarn Plug'n'Play, as the app's bundler sees it. A theme found only through `NODE_PATH` or Node's global folders is no longer taken as installed: `new` and `set base` offer to install it instead of writing a theme the app could not build.

On Windows, `astryx theme build` prints install snippets that import the built theme with a working path. The import path joined the output folder with backslashes and kept a stray one after the dropped `src/`, so the snippet read `import { oceanTheme } from './\themes\ocean/ocean';`, which is not a valid specifier (and `\t` is a tab in a JS string). It now reads `./themes/ocean/ocean` on every platform.

`experimental theme` commands read each folder of Core's sources once while they build Core's component docs. `experimental theme preview app` and `experimental theme preview add` do the same as they write the Overview and Components pages, instead of once per component name. Every run writes and prints the same.

Fix the theme README usage examples to import `Theme` from `@astryxdesign/core/theme` instead of the removed `XDSTheme` alias, and refresh the bundled theme lists in the package index and contributor guide.

From a project subfolder, `theme template` and `theme eject` print a build step that works from that folder (`cd ../.. && … theme build theme.template.ts` when the file is above it), and a blank template path is refused with `theme template` (no path) suggested, which writes at the project root; an absolute template path is told that paths are read from the current folder. `theme build --out` warns that it replaces another source's output only once every output may be written, reads a backslash in `--out` as a folder separator, and its `--check` "Rebuild with" line uses the project's invocation and quotes a path with a space. Building a theme the theme editor made with `theme build` still works, as released, and now warns (once per `--watch` session), naming `experimental theme editor show <theme>`. A theme file that is a link and fails on a relative import is named with the file it points to, with a build of that file that keeps its outputs in the working folder; no load error shows Node's require stack.

A command `theme build` (or `experimental theme compile`) suggests after refusing a source (a Windows-style path, a folder, a file that is not a theme module, or a build output) keeps the `--check`, `--out` and `--icons-specifier` it was given, so following it still checks instead of writing outputs. This holds for a family check, a theme file that is a link, a plain-object family member and a file that changed while loading, and the suggested command is quoted for the shell it runs in (PowerShell too).

The install example `theme build --detail full` (and `experimental theme compile --detail full`) prints says its paths are relative to a file in src/, and now they are, from whichever folder you run it: an output beside src/, such as `themes/ocean/ocean`, is imported as `../themes/ocean/ocean`, not `./themes/ocean/ocean`, which does not resolve from src/. The `theme build --family` snippet uses the same paths and says the same thing in its header.

`theme build` and `experimental theme compile` refuse a theme that sets a private `--_*` variable: the build fails with `ERR_THEME_INVALID` (exit 1, a JSON error envelope) and writes nothing, a `--check` included. Before, it printed the errors and exited 1 but still wrote the outputs and reported `[ok]` and a success receipt, so a reader of the JSON saw a pass.

`theme template` run from a folder inside a project reads its path from that folder within the project root, and with no path writes `theme.template.ts` at the project root, as its help says; a backslash in the path separates folders, as for `theme eject`; `astryx init --features theme`, run below the project root, writes `theme.template.ts` at that root too, because it uses the same template step. Outside any project (no `package.json` in the folder or above it) it writes in the current folder, as released CLIs did, and when it writes the file it warns once on stderr in text mode, naming how to write it at a project root (run it inside a project, or `npm init -y` first); `--json` stays silent. A stale `theme build --check` (and `experimental theme compile --check`) result carries `code: "ERR_THEME_STALE"` beside `upToDate: false`, the code it exits 1 with. A file at an `--out` path that the build did not write is left alone with its real reason and, when one exists, an `--out` path where no output of this build exists yet (a new folder when the theme's module beside it is taken); the build never suggests deleting it. The build-beside-the-source suggestion keeps `--icons-specifier`. `--out` into a folder the theme editor made, for a theme source outside that folder, writes there as released CLIs did, and warns once on stderr in text mode, naming how to keep the editor's folder to its own theme (build beside the source, or pick another `--out`); `--json` stays silent, and `--watch` prints it once per session, not on every rebuild.

`theme build --check` (and `experimental theme compile --check`) names every output the build writes as checked, the `.css.d.ts` stylesheet types too. When the only missing output is a `.css.d.ts` stub, as in projects that keep it out of version control, the check prints one warning line in text mode naming it, and the stub alone does not fail it; `--json` stays silent and the result is unchanged. Every output the check failed on before still fails it, a missing `.d.ts` or `.variants.d.ts` included. `theme eject` into a subfolder of a folder the theme editor made (`themes/g/sub`, where `themes/g/g.settings.json` exists) writes there as released CLIs did, and warns once on stderr in text mode, naming how to keep the editor's folder to its own theme (fork into the project's local themes folder, or pick a path outside the editor's folder); `--json` stays silent and the receipt is unchanged.

The dashboard page template typechecks in an app with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` (it renders the same), so `experimental theme preview add --template dashboard` no longer adds a type error to a strict app. `themeBuild()` no longer takes internal hand-off options for `theme build --watch` or the private-var exit code; `--watch` still warns once per session about a theme editor folder.
`astryx theme template --overwrite` no longer replaces a theme editor file reached through a link to its folder.

TimeInput: `onEntryErrorChange` reports why the field rejects typed text, so an app can word its own message. It receives a `TimeInputEntryError` with a `kind` that does not depend on the locale (`unreadable`, or `outOfRange` for a time before `min` or after `max`), the typed `text`, and, for `outOfRange`, the ISO time `value`. It runs each time the shown rejection changes, including when a new `min`, `max`, or `value`, or disabling the field, changes it, never twice for the same rejection, and with `null` when the rejection ends or the field unmounts while it stands. The native and bottom-sheet surfaces take no typed text, so they never report.

TimeInput, DateTimeInput: a rejected typed time now meets WCAG 2.2 1.4.1 (Use of Color) and 3.3.1 (Error Identification). Before, every draft that was not an accepted time, an unfinished one such as `1` included, was marked invalid and announced on each keystroke, shown only as secondary-color text, and blur reverted it with no message; a native time edit outside `min` or `max` showed no message and its rejection cleared at blur. Now an unfinished time is never flagged: a time outside `min` or `max` shows once it is complete (its hours, both minute digits, both second digits when the field shows seconds, and in 12-hour text its day period unless the hour reads 0 or 13–23), and text that is not a time shows at Enter or blur. The rejected text stays in the field, and a standalone field shows the "Invalid time" message as its error status, with `aria-invalid` and one announcement; inside an InputGroup the rejection sets `aria-invalid` and is announced. Enter in TimeInput and in DateTimeInput's time field commits the typed time and still submits a surrounding form; in DateTimeInput's open preset-time list, Enter picks a time as before. A native time control restores the committed time at blur and keeps its rejection shown. A caller `error` status with a message still shows over the field's message, and the rejection is announced once; a `warning` or `success` status no longer hides a rejection. In DateTimeInput, a date rejection's message comes first and a time rejection under it is announced. What a form posts does not change: while blur keeps a rejected TimeInput draft, a hidden input carries the field's `name` with the committed time.

`TimeInput` and `DateTimeInput`: a bound with no whole minute inside the range keeps its own seconds, so the clamp stays inside the range. Before, `clampTime('12:00','23:59:30')` answered `23:59` — below the minimum the caller set. In a `TimeInput` sheet a wheel rest past such a bound committed nothing; in a `DateTimeInput` sheet, changing the date onto such a bound committed the out-of-range `23:59`. (#10159)

Tooltip's and HoverCard's touch trigger, and Tooltip's handlers with the controlled and enabled flags they carry, sync at commit. After a render React discards, as a suspended transition does, a tap answers with the committed props, and a press outside still closes a shown tooltip.

An installed dependency that ships an Astryx integration manifest which fails to load because a package it requires (a `dependencies` entry or a peer not marked optional) is missing (a broken install) is now reported as that package's integration issue: `component`, `template`, `theme`, `discover` and `search` print the usual one-line warning, and `doctor`'s integration contributions check names it with the load error. Exit codes are unchanged. A command that cannot load also reports why whatever options it was given (`component --list` used to answer "unknown option").

A dry run of `astryx upgrade` no longer tells you to review a `.astryx-conflict` file it has not written. When a copied ShadCN composition conflicts with a newer release, the dry run now says that `--apply` writes the file for review, and an apply still names the file it wrote. The JSON result is unchanged.

`useTruncation` takes `isExpanded`: pass true while the text is shown in full; the hook keeps reporting whether it is cut off when clamped. A Lightbox caption uses it, so its "less" stays while the caption is open.
